Subject: Commercial & Security Exceptions — HelixForge integration (open points)

Hi Sanjay / Priyanka —

Thanks again for the productive call last week. Attached is our consolidated summary of open exceptions across the MSA/DPA/SOW (file: HelixForge_MSA_redlines_v3.pdf) and the Security Matrix that our InfoSec team requested (Security_Matrix.xlsx). High-level asks from Redwood: 

- Confirm whether HelixForge can accept our counter for indemnity/limitation (see section 7.2 in the attached PDF). We proposed a cap tied to 3 months of fees as an equitable compromise.
- SOC 2 report or equivalent — timing and scope (we need the last 12 months).
- Data segregation and retention: can HelixForge limit access to our tenant and support on isolated environments for production PII? See Security Matrix rows 4–6.
- SOW scoping: the initial milestone schedule in the draft SOW is aggressive; request an extra 2 weeks for integration testing and performance tuning.

Can you review and mark items you can accept vs ones you want to propose alternate language for? If helpful we can schedule a 30-min legal sync this week — Vanessa and Karthik will join.

Attachments: HelixForge_MSA_redlines_v3.pdf (redlines), Security_Matrix.xlsx

Thanks,
Lauren Bishop

Hi Lauren —

Thanks for the clear summary and attachments. We did an internal pass and attached our annotated MSA (HelixForge_DPA_annotations_v2.pdf) that highlights the items HelixForge legal would like to keep or adjust. Quick notes: 

- Indemnity/limitation: we understand Redwood's request, and HelixForge is willing to move on the cap if we can keep carveouts for IP infringement claims. Suggest language that excludes third-party open-source litigation exposure from the cap.
- SOC 2: we can provide our most recent SOC 2 Type II report (available). Need to confirm mutual NDA for sharing — will route through Megan.
- Data segregation: we operate multi-tenant clusters; we can propose tenant-level encryption keys and a support playbook for access. Full dedicated tenancy would require commercial terms (cost uplift).
- Retention: we can accept a 90-day default retention window for derived embeddings, with options to extend in the SOW.

We attached our annotated DPA and MSA redlines. We agree to the extra 2 weeks for integration testing.

Would value a short legal call to close the indemnity language. Suggested times: Wed 6/17 9am PT or Thu 6/18 10am PT.

Thanks,
Priyanka Menon
Head of Legal Operations, HelixForge
priyanka@helixforge.com

Attachments: HelixForge_DPA_annotations_v2.pdf

Looping in Karthik (legal) — forwarding HelixForge's annotated redlines. High-level internal read: HelixForge is willing to move on most commercial items but will push on the IP carveout in indemnity and on dedicated tenancy.

My suggested approach: 
- Accept a capped indemnity at 3 months' fees but add carveouts for IP-specific litigation only if we insist on broader remedies elsewhere (we should not open an uncapped exposure). Karthik: can your team propose a short clause that preserves our position while giving HelixForge limited IP carveout?
- For SOC2 and logs: request SOC2 Type II and an agreed timeframe to produce the report (within 5 business days of countersignature). If they cannot produce, require quarterly attestations until one is provided.
- Data segregation: accept tenant-level encryption + strict access playbook as a baseline. Dedicated tenancy must be an SOW-priced optional add-on.

If legal is comfortable, we can offer the 3-month cap with the above mitigations to get to signature next week — the integration schedule depends on this.

Thanks for the context — reviewed the redlines. Short guidance from Legal: 

- Indemnity cap: Redwood legal can accept 3 months' fees as a cap, provided we keep an explicit carveout for gross negligence and willful misconduct, and we limit IP carveouts strictly to direct infringement (no broad open-source carveouts). Proposed language: cap = lesser of 3 months fees or actual direct damages; carveouts = gross negligence, willful misconduct, direct IP infringement. I'll draft this and share a tracked clause by EOD.
- IP indemnity: HelixForge's request to exclude open-source claims from the cap is not acceptable in broad form. We can accept a narrow exclusion limited to pre-approved OSS components listed in an appendix.
- Evidence delivery: SOC2 Type II — HelixForge to provide the latest report within 5 business days of countersignature; if not available, provide a remediation plan and quarterly attestations.
- Data access: tenant-level encryption + access playbook accepted. If they want dedicated tenancy, it goes in SOW as a paid option.

Action items: Vanessa/Lauren — confirm you want me to send the redlined clause to Megan & Priyanka for final review, or do you prefer a 30-min call? I can do either.

Karthik Iyer
Senior Counsel, Redwood Inference
karthik.iyer@redwood.inference.com

Lauren / team —

Thanks for the quick turnaround and clarity. We're aligned on most items and appreciate the constructive compromise on indemnity. We've uploaded a final redline of the DPA and a short note on SOW scoping (attached: HelixForge_DPA_annotations_v2.pdf). Key confirmations: 

- Indemnity: HelixForge can accept the 3-month cap if Redwood accepts the narrow OSS appendix approach for pre-approved components. We'll list the components in an appendix and keep IP carveouts scoped to direct infringement.
- SOC2: we'll share the latest report with Megan (cc) once the mutual NDA is complete — target 3 business days after countersignature.
- Retention: OK with 90-day default for derived embeddings; please confirm SOW language for longer retention for customers that require it.
- Commercial: we accept the 2-week extension for testing and will update milestone dates in the SOW.

Next steps: Priyanka and Megan will review Karthik's draft clause once received. If that aligns, we can exchange final counters and move to DocuSign. Please confirm if Redwood wants the dedicated-tenancy pricing included in the SOW as an optional line item.

Attachments: HelixForge_DPA_annotations_v2.pdf

Best,
Sanjay Rao
